params.body:
## Why

The `settings` row `api_key` is the remove.bg API key, and it sat in plain text. `updateBackground`
wrote `$request['api_key']` straight into the row, `App\Http\Helpers\Photo` read the raw value, and
`settings/setting/_tabs/removebg.blade.php` rendered it as the value of a plain `x-ui.input` — not
even `type="password"`. So the key was readable in any dump, any backup and any read on that table,
it was readable on screen over the shoulder of whoever opened the pane, and it travelled to every
browser that did and back on every save. remove.bg is a paid, per-credit account, so that key is
worth stealing: whoever has it spends the credits.

Same shape as #261 (Car-Pass) and #258 (RealGarant), and it is the one #261 named as "also worth a
decision, not touched here". This is that decision.

## What

- **`App\Support\RemoveBgKey`** is the one place the key is resolved and the one place it is turned
  into what gets stored. `resolve()` is the reading `Photo` does (the stored row, whichever row
  holds it, else the env key); `forDealer()` is the reading `stocklist:smoke` does (this dealer's
  own row, else the env key). Both decrypt the stored value. `forStorage()` is what the controller
  writes. Nothing else reads `api_key` any more: a grep over `app/`, `resources/`, `routes/` and
  `tests/` leaves the settings key only inside this class, the Nederland Mobiel constant in
  `IntegrationCredentials` (a different credential that happens to share the substring), the
  OpenAI/WhatsApp/AutoConnect `services.*.api_key` config reads, the `X-Api-Key` header of the
  public API, and the `settings.api_key` translation label.
- **A sibling class rather than a fourth credential in `App\Support\IntegrationCredentials`** (#256),
  and the reason is the resolution order. That class exists for PLATFORM credentials and resolves
  the environment FIRST, because a VWE account belongs in the environment and the settings row is
  only a fallback until the env is filled. remove.bg is the other way round: it is a per-dealer
  setting a dealer may type in themselves, the stored row WINS over `REMOVEBG_API_KEY`, and the env
  key is the platform's fallback for a dealer who never entered one. Extending the env-first
  resolver with a `removeBgKey()` that "prefers config" would have silently stopped honouring a
  dealer's own key the moment the platform key is set — which is exactly the per-dealer key the
  brief says must keep working as it does today. On top of that, `RemoveBgKey` carries the
  migration's conversion rule (as `CarpassPassword` does for #261), which no credential in
  `IntegrationCredentials` has.
- **Controller.** `SettingsController::updateBackground` encrypts on the way in and keeps the stored
  key when nothing was typed. That already was the behaviour of the `!= ''` guard, and it has to
  stay: this pane is a single form that also carries the two background images, so an empty key
  field is the normal state of every save that only changes a picture.
- **View.** The pane renders an empty `x-ui.password` and says under it, in the `help` slot of
  `x-ui.field`, which of the two states you are in: "Er is een sleutel ingesteld. Laat leeg om ze te
  behouden." / "Nog geen sleutel ingesteld.", in nl/en/fr/de/es (`settings.api_key_hint_set` /
  `_unset`). Whether something is stored is read from the value the controller already passes to the
  view, never decrypted there, so a row that has not been through the migration yet cannot make the
  pane throw. `es/settings.php` had no `api_key` label at all and now has one.
- **Readers.** `Photo::old_remove_background` and `IntegrationSmoke::checkRemovebg` go through the
  resolver. Neither changes which key it picks; both now get the plain key instead of the raw
  column.
- **`CUTOVER.md`.** The line #261 added is widened to cover both credentials rather than a second
  line appearing next to it, since it is one `migrate --force` and one rule.

## Migration safety

`2026_09_13_000200_encrypt_removebg_api_key`. The cutover loads a fresh production dump on the same
box with the SAME `APP_KEY` and Forge runs `migrate --force` after it, so this migration has to
survive a table that is plaintext again and it has to be safe to run twice.

- **No column change, and that is checked, not assumed.** `settings`.`value` is `text` in
  `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql`, so a payload of a few hundred characters has room to spare.
  (#261 had to widen `dealers.carpass_password` from `varchar(255)` first; here there is nothing to
  widen and therefore nothing that can be truncated into an unreadable key.)
- **"Already encrypted?" is a real decrypt attempt**, `Crypt::decryptString()` in a try/catch, not a
  match on the `eyJpdiI6` prefix. The payload is base64 of a JSON object, so the prefix is a
  heuristic and a key that happened to start that way would be skipped forever. The prefix is used
  only as a fast path in the safe direction: something that does not start with it cannot be a
  payload, so there is nothing to try.
- **The write is a raw query builder update**, chunked with `chunkById`, 200 at a time, skipping
  `null` and `''`, and scoped to `key = 'api_key'` so no other setting is touched.
- **A row that is still plaintext keeps working.** Between loading the dump and running the
  migration that is the normal state, and a reader that insisted on ciphertext would take remove.bg
  down for that window. A row that looks like a payload but does not open (a different `APP_KEY`) is
  logged and read as "not stored", so the caller falls through to `REMOVEBG_API_KEY` instead of
  sending a base64 blob to remove.bg as a credential.
- The rule lives in `App\Support\RemoveBgKey::encryptPlaintextRows()`, not inside the migration
  closure, so it can be called twice in a test. A rule that cannot be run again cannot be proven to
  be idempotent.
- `down()` is deliberately empty: decrypting back to plaintext would undo the point.

## Checked

- `./vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='RemoveB|Removebg|RemoveBgKey|Photo|SettingsTab|SmokeTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest|UiApiUsageTest|ClassReferencesResolveTest|IntegrationCredentials|IntegrationSmoke|CarpassPassword|WarrantyPassword|CompiledViews|BuildContract'`
  against a local MySQL loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the migrations after the
  dump: **186 tests, 1042 assertions, green**, `RemoveBackgroundTest` included. The route smoke test
  renders the settings page, so the new pane markup is covered there too.
- `php artisan migrate --force` on that database with a plaintext `api_key` row present: the
  migration runs and the row comes out as a payload. Deleting only its `migrations` entry and
  running it again leaves the stored value byte for byte identical, so nothing is encrypted twice.
- `APP_KEY=... php artisan view:cache` plus `php -l` over every compiled view, the compiled pane
  included: clean. `php -l` on every changed PHP file and on the five `settings.php` language files.
- New tests in `tests/Feature/RemoveBgKeyTest.php` (16): the pane contains neither the key nor its
  ciphertext and the field is a `type="password"` with an empty value; the hint matches the state;
  an empty submit and a missing field both keep the stored key; a typed key is stored encrypted (the
  raw column differs from what was typed, the resolver returns what was typed); the stored key beats
  the env key and the env key is used when nothing is stored; nowhere set is `null` and not an empty
  key; a row that is still plaintext is read as it is; an undecryptable row falls back to the env
  key; the dealer reading prefers the dealer's own row; `Photo::old_remove_background` calls
  remove.bg with the DECRYPTED key (HTTP faked, `X-Api-Key` asserted); the conversion over a mix of
  plaintext, ciphertext, empty and null rows converts only the plaintext one, converts nothing on a
  second run and touches no other setting key; and a value with the right prefix that is not a
  payload is not mistaken for one.

## Reported, not touched

`updateBackground` looks the row up with `first(['key' => 'api_key'])`, without a dealer scope, so a
save by one dealer can overwrite another dealer's row — and `Photo` reads the first `api_key` row it
finds, whatever dealer it belongs to, because it runs from a queued job with no logged-in user, so a
dealer's own key can be charged for another dealer's photo. That is older than this change and
narrowing it here would move which account is billed rather than fix anything, so both readings were
kept exactly as they were. Worth a decision of its own.
params.title: remove.bg: the API key is encrypted at rest
